analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bayern are unbeaten (two wins, two draws) and won 2-0 at Atlético on matchday 4, but they are only 13th, so they need wins like this to climb into the top eight. Slavia are 34th with one point after losing 2-1 to Arsenal, though they pushed them to the end. Slavia were without the suspended Tomas Chory and the injured Igoh Ogbu for that game; Chory's ban has been served. I found no recent Bayern injury news, so their team news is a gap to fill later.

goals.text: The numbers say 5.1 goals, 4.5 of them Bayern's. I lean lower: Slavia have not been thrashed this season (2-1 against Arsenal, 3-2 against Lens), and their predicted line-up has three centre-backs and wing-backs, which makes it harder to run up big scores. Bayern's 3-3 with Viking shows they will concede chances too.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.0 corners, 8.2 of them Bayern's. I lean higher: Slavia's back five will sit deep and block crosses, which turns into corners, and Bayern will need goals for goal difference in a tight race for the top eight.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean slightly lower: one-sided games like this rarely get heated, and Bayern's possession means Slavia spend more time defending in shape than chasing. Slavia's own record (Chory suspended earlier) is the one thing pushing the other way.

shots.text: The numbers say 37 shots, 28 of them Bayern's. I would leave it: Bayern will dominate, but Slavia's deep block will block many efforts. Both effects are already priced in.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 14 shots on target. I lean lower: a crowded penalty area means more blocked and off-target attempts, and Slavia showed against Arsenal that they can keep a game close. Bayern should still have nine or ten on target.
